This rapid intervention corps which consisted of Spanish and some other forces. It was under command of a French general and the Chief of Staff was an American general, General Sylvester. The corps commander carried out operations against my forces from the area of Duvansko Polje [phoen]. They were using ammunition with white signs on it. Croats did not have such ammunition or the amounts that were used. Chief of Staff, General Sylvester was supporting the Muslims during the Sarajevo offensive that started in June, and where the positions from Mount Igman were used to fire against Serbian positions around Sarajevo. In the period between the 29th of August and the 14th of September, there were intense NATO Alliance combat activities, not of UNPROFOR, but of the NATO Alliance, against units of the VRS. At a later stage, I heard that 110 civilians were also killed somewhere in Eastern Bosnia, but I don't know much about that, because I wasn't paying much attention to that. So these 15 days of air-strikes was something that I will use a specific expression, allegedly Markale II, but the real intention was to defeat the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document. In the meantime, let me call the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... It will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D774 shall be assigned exhibit number D258, marked for identification, pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please have 1D767 now on the screen so that we can see what the consequences of the operations discussed a moment ago were and to see how VRS was being prevented from resisting the attacks against them. This is a document issued by the Main Staff of the VRS dated 9th of September. It is about the changes in the system of communications and courier services. An order. And I quote: "Because of the problems caused by air-strikes of the NATO against radio-relay hubs and postal telegraph and telephone facilities and communications facilities in the areas of responsibility of Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, Herzegovina Corps, Drina Corps and East Bosnia Corps, and until alternative lines of communications are established with the purpose of more urgent and better-organised sending and receiving of telegraphs and written information, I order: "1. Establish a temporary forward office of the Main Staff of the VRS at the command post of the East Bosnia Corps for the purpose of receiving all types of written documents, telegrams and written documents, issued by the forward command post 1 of the Main Staff of the VRS, 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps, military schools, the 14th Logistics Base, the 1st Motorised Rocket" -- It is very difficult to read this. "And the 35th Logistics Base ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And this is my question to you, General: Were you also required to organise courier service between you and the Main Staff from the location where you were at the forward command post because all communications system within the republic was disrupted and we could not use phones, telegraph or anything else? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 9th of September, a simultaneous attack was carried out against all 13 communication hubs in the VRS. All of our communication hubs. And that was the first time during the war that we did not have radio or telegraph communications. I remember this document really well because I was asked to set up this office in Banja Luka and not in Bijeljina, but I could not accept that because the fate of Banja Luka was not secure. Operation Storm may have continued. Tudjman was saying that he intends to drink coffee in Hotel Banja Luka and I didn't want to be the one who had to make this coffee for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can we please have this 1D767 entered into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we come to that, I would like to clarify something. I can't see the date in the heading of this page. Could that be enlarged, please. It seems to be the 6th of September, 1995. In your list of documents, you have listed it as a document from the 3rd of September, 1995. That -- I just want to clarify that. And I would like to put a question to the witness. This document, obviously from the 6th of September, how does it relate to the 9th of September? You just testified that there was an attack -- the first attack on -- against all 13 communication hubs in the VRS. The 9th of September should be a date after this document was drafted and sent. Could you please help to clarify that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the screen before me, it is hard to tell whether it's the 6th or the 8th. The air-strike took place on the 9th or, rather, the air-strikes started on the 24th of August, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 29th of August.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And lasted until 14th of September. I remember the air-strike that was carried out on the 9th because then all communications were interrupted. I remember having a discussion with Mladic about what to do if the command post gets destroyed and how to organise the office for receiving and sending of mail. Initially the idea was to do it in Banja Luka, and I explained why not there. But we still had communications up until the 9th, and, on that day, the repeater near Mrkonjic Grad was destroyed. I had a visitor, two bishops, rather, Atanasije Jevtic, and another bishop. So that's how I remember the air-strike against our repeater. It does not matter when the air-strike was carried out. Commander may have expected this air-strike, but this one huge simultaneous air-strike against all repeaters was on the 9th and I even had two soldiers who were casualties of the air-strike, because they were at the repeater at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. The document will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D767 shall be assigned exhibit number D259, marked for identification, pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have 1D770, please. A report about a press conference. We do have a translation. There's also a cassette we received from the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document drafted on 26th September 1995. And in there, we have all the NATO operations enumerated for the entire period of the air-strikes. And that's why the order was issued, the order that was in the previous document. I will only quote the sixth paragraph thereof, starting with the words: "International community ..." "According to the Vance Plan, the international community gave guarantees for safety of the Serbian people in the Republika Srpska of Krajina but failed to fulfil them. We are witnessing the consequences of such an aggression which resulted in the greatest ethnic cleansing in this century in Europe. It was done to the Serbian people and a part of the international community offered assistance and support to Croatia in doing it. "More than 700.000 Serbs were driven away from the ancient territories and all their estates were robbed and burned down. At the same time, the members of the Croatian Armed Forces committed mass crimes throughout the Republika Srpska Krajina. At the press conference, there was also mention of the units that were fighting against VRS and also against Republika Srpska Krajina." Were you informed about the events discussed there, and was the Croatian population informed about the fact that in the enter period of the war, UNPROFOR and NATO sided with the Croats and the Muslim army? Thank you. Can you please tell us whether the international community did anything to prevent this?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, do I have to answer this question? Because I believe I have already answered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you have already answered it, it's fine. Indeed, there are some repetitions in answering. Mr. Tolimir, the witness refers to his previous answer. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Since the witness told us that he already answered the question, I would like to tender this document, 1D770. This will save us some time as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I would object until we can get some more information on where this came from. It doesn't have an ERN on it, and so if the General could tell us where it came from, where he got it, I -- we don't see the bottom of it either, so we need some basics on something like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we please scroll down or go to the next page. Is there another page? It isn't. Mr. Milovanovic, do you know this document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But I am familiar with the contents of the document. I was familiar with the contents throughout the whole war because it had to do with the answer that Tolimir wanted me to give him the answer if NATO supported the Muslims, and I already answered that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. I want to know if you are familiar with this document on the screen. Do you know anything about a press conference at that time, 26th of February, 1995, given by the commander. Commander-in-Chief.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He had a lot of press conferences. I don't know if I knew of this one or not. I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you help us with the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The document was given along with the video cassette containing footage of that conference, and this is an original translation, in order to inform the public about what was happening -- the international public, about what was going on during the war in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said the document was given. By whom?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a cassette that was provided by the Prosecution, and it's in the archives. It's a video cassette of a press conference that is in evidence. And then there is an original translation of the document attached with this, and this was done by the General Gvero Defence, I think. Because this is his document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's -- doesn't tell us anything. If -- if it is -- if there is an cassette that was provided by the Prosecution in a previous case, there'll be a number, and if they could tell us that number, then we can -- then we're fine. If it's something -- and I -- General Gvero sometimes got material from his own sources, so if it's one of those, we need to know where it came from, who provided it, and that's just, of course, normal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you give more information, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I am taking into account what the Prosecutor said. We are going to check when the cassette was disclosed and what the number was, and we're going to provide all this information in the course of the next few days so that we don't lose any more time on that in the courtroom at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: More important is to know the convenience -- the provenance of this document on the screen you are tendering. But we will wait for additional information. You may come back to that. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can we have 1D773 now, please. So that we don't lose any more time here, we can see a document drafted by this witness. We can see the witness's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So my question is: Is this a document that you drafted at the General -- at the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, and is this your signature? Is this the document that you referred to during the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signature is mine, and what I am seeing on the last page of the document indicates that that is my work. It's a description by the Main Staff, or of the Main Staff. I gave that to the Prosecution last week, and they said that they would show it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the first page of this document. Can we show the witness the first page so that we can finish with this document, in order to be rational with the time that we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we have a different document on the screen. We need the first page of 1D773.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 772.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we were looking at the -- at a page - I don't know which one - of 1D773. But this is page 9, obviously, of a document. We don't have a different -- other pages, 1 through 8. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the correct number is 1D772. Mr. Tolimir made an error. It was a slip of the tongue. He said 773. So I see that there is some confusion in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, 1D772 is not on the list of documents to be used. Yes, it is. Sorry. Undated document from VRS headquarters; I see that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, if you look at this document and headings and subheadings, we're looking at the heading: The forming of the Main Staff. On page 12, during the examination-in-chief, line 1, you said something about how the Army of Republika Srpska is going to be formed; and you also talked about those being put forward by the commander for different posts. Can you tell us if you remember that, and if this is the document that you wrote and handed over to the Prosecution? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember everything. This is a document that I wrote. I can tell also by the fact that my printer is always printing at an angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us whether you talked about the content of the document during the examination-in-chief so that we can tendered this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave answers to the Prosecutor's questions regarding the organisation and structure of the Main Staff, and all of that was based on what is in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender 177 -- 1D772 so that we don't have to put questions again to the witness that he already answered during the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we please see the last page of this document? Yes, page 9 with a signature. Mr. Milovanovic, when did you draft and write this text of nine pages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wrote this text last year on the occasion of Army Day of the Army of Republika Srpska. There was a round-table in Banja Luka that was held about the establishment and the development of the Army of Republika Srpska, and it was my task, as the war Chief of the Main Staff, to write about two topics. One topic was the Main Staff. I had to write a presentation nine pages long. And then another topic, the Creation and Development of the Army of Republika Srpska, and that presentation was supposed to be 12 pages long. I did respect or keep to that number of pages, and I gave both of those presentations to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, just to finish up the orientation. As the General -- he just gave those to us a few days ago, so we copied them and gave them to the Defence, and that's how they came into our possession and into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document, 1D772, will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was just, during our discussion, uploaded into e-court. I mean the English translation. We should have a look on the screen. And to see it. Thank you very much. It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D772 shall be assigned exhibit number D260. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could I ask the e-court now to show 1D771, please, in relation to which the witness said just a little bit earlier, that he wrote it. So to avoid repetition, can we now look at the first page and then I'm going to put a question. The document is: The creation and the development of the Army of Republika Srpska during the defence homeland war in Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1992 to 1995. It was written by General Manojlo Milovanovic, the wartime Chief of the Main Staff of the VRS, Colonel-General, retired. Can we now visually show the rest of the pages now, including the last page of this document. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President. And thank you to e-court. Mr. President, since the witness said a little bit earlier that he presented this document at the same time as the other one, I would just like the witness to confirm whether this is a document that he wrote and handed over to the Prosecution, and I would like to tender this into evidence because this document was referred to during the examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document that I wrote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is English translation available?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Almost. It's -- the revision, I think, is being worked on. So I think in the next day or so, we should have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The document will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D771 shall be assigned exhibit number D261, marked for identification, pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would ask for 65 ter 04071 to be shown. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, sir, we can see now a document by the Main Staff, intelligence and security sector, of the 28th of July, 1995. It's an intelligence report which states, I am quoting from the first paragraph: "The west continues to threaten Serbs, demonstrate their force and provide political and diplomatic support to the Croat-Muslim offensive operations, as well as political and diplomatic support to the Croat-Muslim offensive operations." Thank you, General. "At this stage, they are focussed on protecting the Muslim enclaves of Gorazde and Sarajevo and it is not being ruled out that they will use force to protect the so-called Bihac safe area. They demonstrate determination to use force in case that delivery of humanitarian assistance is obstructed." And then paragraph 2: "The plan of NATO air force operations in the area of Bihac is being mapped out, but a number of sources indicate that the situation in Cazin Krajina is vague and that the use of NATO forces is not very likely." General, sir, did you receive this information from the intelligence and security sector at the forward command post and do you recall receiving information of this type? Did this information arrive on a daily basis at the forward command post where you were located? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information did not reach the forward command post. It reached the command of the 2nd Corps where I would hand them over. I simply did not want to open an office for incoming and outgoing mail at the forward command post. I'm sorry that I cannot read all of this report to see if there was information that day about me losing Grahovo and Glamoc with my units that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the last page of this document. This is page 4 in the English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And you can see this last page now. It was sent out to everyone. And it states: "The Army of the Independent State of Croatia regrouped their forces in the directions leading to the western parts of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina. Units are at full combat readiness, and prepared to start an attack immediately. They think that the Army of Yugoslavia will not react and they are spreading information that the SVK will not be allowed to launch attacks in Baranja, Easter Slavonia and Western Srem or move the present line of engagement." Chief Major-General Zdravko Tolimir, and it also states this was sent to IKM 1 the forward command post of the Army of Republika Srpska to such and such a person. The name is not mentioned here but was that you, who were there at IKM 1 of the Main Staff of the VRS and perhaps this is something that actually stands in for your first and last name, in a kind of code?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My forward command post was command post number 1. I can see that you had 2 and 3 in Eastern Bosnia. I don't know to whom this was addressed but, in any event, the document did reach me, either through the IKM or through the 2nd Corps command. I don't know what I'm supposed to answer, whether I'd seen the document before or ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My first question, before you asked to look at the last page was this. The West, in this offensive by the Muslims and Croats, which was being conducted even from the territory of Croatia against the Army of Republika Srpska, state political, diplomatic, and all other kinds of threats towards Republika Srpska at that particular time and supported the Muslim army, the Croat army, and the army of the Republic of Croatia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about that already when I talked about the support of the Euro Corps to the Croatian army. So my answer remains yes. But from what I can see, you are again trying to blame the West. I actually would blame the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia more than the West because the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was obliged to guarantee or to support the Vance Plan, and it even said in one provision, even at the cost of use of force or arms. So practically Yugoslavia was supposed to declare war against Croatia. But it failed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. You also wanted to see if the information covered the status of the Glamoc and Grahovo front.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at page 2 in e-court. Paragraph 5. This is the following page in the English in the e-court, and we can see here where it says:

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "The Ustasha forces" --

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Ustashas started --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "The Ustasha offensive in the direction of Kupres started on 29 July 1995 with heavy artillery support and the focus on (illegible). In the direction of Grahovo and Glamoc, they're carrying out fortification works at the reach [as interpreted] lines and bringing in fresh forces in order to carry out combat operations for relief of units" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't receive interpretation at the moment. Please slow down and read what you want to read.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Considering the fact that they did not get in contact with our units at that part of the front, offensive activities are likely to continue in the direction of Glamoc, Sipovo, Jajce, and Grahovo - Knin."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: This information, did it report realistically on the state of affairs that they were already fortifying in Glamoc and Grahovo and that they were planning further actions from those locations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And thank you for that information, because all along I thought that no one cared about my situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We must have our second break now, Mr. Tolimir. We will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I wanted to seek to tender this document just before the break. Hence, I'm tendering it now so as to be able to move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 4071 shall be assigned exhibit number D262. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we next have 65 ter 04081. I wanted to say for the transcript that it's a Main Staff of the VRS document, dated the 6th of October, 1995. It is the text of the agreement on the cessation of hostilities. It was forwarded to those specified on a different page. This document was signed by Major-General Zdravko Tolimir. And I quote: "Please find attached the integral text of the cease-fire agreement in the former BiH which will come into effect at 0000 [as interpreted] hours on 10 October 1995. Signed by Major-General Zdravko Tolimir." Thank you. We can see the text of the cease-fire agreement for BiH dated the 5th of October, 1995. There are no further comments. And it was forwarded to the end users. It also refers to the end of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In the first paragraph, a cease-fire is discussed, as well as in the second. The third paragraph refers to the implementation of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: Was this agreement forwarded to the forward command post and did all units within your area of responsibility abide by it?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agreement was forwarded to the forward command post, but the Muslim side did not honour it. At the time of its coming into effect, we lost the last town we held on to in the Bosnian Krajina in the west, which is Bosanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Tell us briefly how did the international community react to it, and did they try to return the Muslim side to their initial positions as they existed before the agreement was signed?

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not feel the reaction of the international community because having lost Sanski Most I was forced to disband the 2nd Krajina Corps following a decision that was made by the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this be admitted into evidence, please. And then we can move on to the next issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to see the list of addressees of this document and the signature block. The last page. The end of the page. This seems to be the last page. Mr. Milovanovic, can you help us? You stated that you received it at the forward command post, if I'm not mistaken. Do you know to whom this document was sent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who it was sent to. I read it at the command post of the 2nd Corps at the time it still existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we should just clarify. I don't know if the General, I don't think he said it, but I think the 2nd Corps, I think he meant the 2nd Krajina Corps, just not to be mixed up with another 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Milovanovic, perhaps you can help us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I said the 2nd Krajina Corps. The only thing I can add is of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Sometimes during the interpretation something is missed -- something is missing. We can't verify where it was sent to; nevertheless, we will receive it as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter document 4081 shall be assigned exhibit number D263. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we please have 65 ter 05834 shown in e-court. We can see it. It's a Main Staff document of the VRS, dated the 11th of October. It was sent by courier because the communications lines were down. The same thing applied to the agreement on the cessation of hostilities. That is why there are no other signatures than of the person who sent it. This has to do with blocking the enemy offensive on the western RS front. Order by the commander of the Main Staff. Could we please go to the last page to see the commander's signature? Page 2 in the Serbian, which is difficult to read. In any case, it reads: "Commander, Colonel General Ratko Mladic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We tried to believe it, although we can't really make it out. Oh, there's another page now. In the translation and in the B/C/S version on the screen, we can see now it is said: "General Pukovnik, Ratko Mladic."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If we look at page 1 -- actually, the first paragraph on this page, it reads: "Chief of the Main Staff of the VRS, Lieutenant-General Manojlo Milovanovic is to manage the entire operation and coordinate combat activities of the corps, operational groups, and brigades from the forward command post of the Main Staff of the VRS in Banja Luka." Next we have specified what each of the assistants was to do, in order to stabilize the front lines. Could we go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, can you tell us whether you received this commander's order? And what can you tell us about the way the forces were stabilized, meaning to say those that were under your command.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive this order by mail or courier, because I drafted it, together with General Mladic. We were together at the forward command post. There was some discussion as to why I was to command, when he was there, but you know well that by that time he was an ill man. This was the final stage of defensive operations of Banja Luka when we had to pull out the 30th Division to the Ugar river. That was the last stand, so to speak, and we managed to complete our task. I received this order orally from General Mladic and later on he must have converted it into written form, as I can see now. I believe I discussed the issue of Mladic appointing certain assistants of his to command specific parts of the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document. And next I would like to have 1D618 shown in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter document 5834 shall be assigned exhibit number D264. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't see you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General Tolimir had put in the record that this was not a teletyped document, it was a couriered document. If we could have some foundation in the record, I would appreciate it, since he has offered it now into evidence because it looked like a teletyped document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you referring to the last one we admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then we should have it back on the screen, D264, page 1 in both versions. I was going to ask Mr. Tolimir as well about this -- the source of this comment. But, you see, behind the words "very urgent," "deliver by courier." I think Mr. Tolimir was referring to this part of the document. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That's all I needed. I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Problem resolved. Let's move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D618, please. It is it another Main Staff document of January 1, 1995, sent to all commands. The title is: Implementation of the agreement on complete cessation of hostilities with the Muslim side, order. I seek to tender it so as to show that the agreement that was forwarded in its original form and was not admitted was implemented by virtue of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, did you see or receive this order, and did you implement it? Do the contents of the document jog your memory as to some activities you managed during the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could just get the basics of what this says, just who -- who it is to, what the subject matter is. Then I don't need the whole thing read, of course, but that doesn't -- the question doesn't help us at all if we have no idea what this is. Just a brief idea of what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, that would be helpful. We don't have the English translation and don't know anything about that. And your comment, "I seek to tender it so as to show that the agreement that was forwarded in its original form." I don't understand what are you referring to. This was page 70, lines 12 and 13. Please help to us understand, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'll try. This is a Main Staff document of the VRS dated the 1st of January. It was very urgent, delivered to the commands of all the units as specified here, per establishment. Personally to their commanders or Chiefs of Staff. The title is: Implementation of the agreement on the complete cessation of hostilities with the Muslim side, order. It reads in the first paragraph: "On 31st of December, 1995, an agreement was signed on a complete cessation of hostilities between the forces of the RS and Muslim forces in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina." I wanted to have this document admitted to corroborate the other document where we did not know who it was sent to. It was something we used a moment ago. I believe it was 65 ter 04081, and it was forwarded to the units, much the same way as this one. It concerned the same topic, which is cessation of hostilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could the witness please tell us whether he, too, as the chief of the Main Staff, received this document and whether he acted by it.

utterances.speaker: MANOJLO MILOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This agreement has no apparent connection to the previous one. This is agreement on a four-month truce, the so-called Carter truce, and we have discussed it already this morning. The other agreement we saw a moment ago, dated the 10th of October, is the agreement on the cessation of hostilities. I believe you used an inexpert phrase when YOU said that it was agreement on the end of the war, but that was obviously wrong. The war in Bosnia and Herzegovina actually never ended because such a decision was not formally made. All I can say about this is that I know that it was not honoured by the Muslim agreement. This was an agreement between us and the Muslims. The other warring factions, that is to say, the Croats, were not included. The other agreement we saw a moment ago is an agreement on cessation of hostilities in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, meaning it encompassed all of the warring parties. Practically speaking, that was the agreement about the end of the war, and it was drafted in order to pave a way for the Dayton peace talks. You may remember that we then flew to Belgrade together because Mladic was unable to take that flight. We were there to meet the leadership of the FRY to harmonise our positions as Milosevic had been appointed as the head of the Serb delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Thank you for correcting me. I showed you the agreement of the 1st of January, 1995, thinking that it was actually the one from the 1st of October and that is an error that created the confusion. Now you have clarified that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this document, 1D618, could we please have that admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm still slightly confused. We have now figured out, due to the assistance of Mr. Milovanovic, that there were two different instances, in January, and in October. But what is this document about? I don't understand B/C/S. I can't read it. I have no idea. I don't know who signed it, what is the content, if this is an attachment. We just see one page. And I really don't know what it is about. It seems to have something to do with an agreement from the 1st of January, 1995, but that's all I know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, sir, are you able to tell the Trial Chamber if this is an order by the commander on the implementation of the agreement that was signed on the 1st of January, 1995, and that's why we have two documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask e-court to show the first page to the General so that he could see it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The agreement that we're looking at right now from the 1st of January, 1995 does not have any physical or other connection with the agreement of the 10th of October. This agreement that we're looking at right now of the 1st of January is of a limited scope and only refers to Serbs and Muslims in Western Bosnia, in the Bihac area, thus. An attempt by the international community to save Bihac or to keep it under the Muslim control and to prevent the Serbian forces from taking it. The second agreement of the 10th of October is a comprehensive one, including the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it is aimed at ending the war among all the warring parties, among the Serbs, the Croats, the Muslims and NATO, wherever they were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: General, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D618. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the witness said it only refers to Serbs and Muslims in Western Bosnia in the Bihac area. What is the relevance of this document to our case here in this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. It doesn't have to be tendered, because the document signed by the Muslims on the cessation of hostilities of the 1st of January 1995 was not admitted with your explanation that you don't know what that document was about. But I don't have any need to have it admitted. I mean, it's already here, and that's why I suggested it be tendered. If not, well, never mind. I'm just going to put my final questions to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you are not able to help us to understand the relation between our case and the Bihac area, then you should move on. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I see that the problem is in the lack of translation of the document. The document clearly states that this is about the implementation of the order on the complete cessation of hostilities and that is the agreement which was admitted, and it has number P1011. So this is an order seeking the implementation of that agreement on the Serbian side, or by the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Milovanovic, is that your understanding of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the lawyer, if he could, to just repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I would just like to point to the first paragraph which states that: "On the 31st of December, 1994 agreement was signed on the complete cessation of hostilities between the forces of the RS and the Muslim forces in the former BiH."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. I have understood the lawyer right now. It's correct. It states in the territory of the former BiH. However, this morning I already talked about this document. That agreement was not honoured. That is the Carter agreement. It was not honoured. It was violated already on the 13th of January by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Milovanovic, of course, you told us about that. The question was a different one. Is this an order of General Mladic to implement the agreement we have seen signed by Izetbegovic, Karadzic in the presence of Mr. Akashi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if Akashi was present, but I know that Jimmy Carter was. He was the organiser of the negotiations in the actual signing of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the absence of a clarification, we will mark it for identification, and we will come back to that later.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D618 shall be assigned exhibit number D265, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovanovic, for coming to testify before this Tribunal. Thank you for everything. Excuse me, for putting questions that may have caused some confusion like this last one was. Thank you for all your clarifications and assistance during your testimony. I'm wishing you a safe return home. May God bless you. I hope you enjoy your deserved retirement since you were at the most exposed part of the front, the most difficult part in Republika Srpska, and I wanted to ask you if there's anything that you like to say that I did not ask you but that you would like to take the opportunity and say now? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, this is it not a proper conducting of a cross-examination. If you have no more questions, then it's fine that this will be the end of your cross-examination. I take it you're finished your cross-examination, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. You are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would like to wish General Milovanovic a safe and blessed return home to his family and this is all the questions that the Defence has for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey, your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir, you will be pleased that this concludes your testimony here in this trial. Thank you very much that you were able to come again to The Hague and to undergo such a lengthy experience. Thank you very much for your attendance here. You may now return to your normal activities. There is no possibility to start with the next witness. We have to adjourn for the week, and we will resume on Monday in the afternoon, 2.15 in this courtroom. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
